findings.scenario: A reviewer types into the Reviewer note textarea; the note state is passed straight into dangerouslySetInnerHTML and executes as HTML on the next render.
findings.impact: Arbitrary HTML and script injection from fully reviewer-controlled input; the payload runs in the application origin on every render of the note preview instead of being rendered as plain text.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with Semgrep rule react-dangerous-html-review against the review head: ActionComposer.tsx:31 renders the dynamic note state through dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: note }} with no sanitization, so it is a true positive unlike SafeAnnouncement whose input is a source-controlled constant; React auto-escapes text children, so the confirmed fix renders {note} as text.
findings.fix:
Replace the dangerouslySetInnerHTML preview in src/components/ActionComposer.tsx with a plain React text child:
{note}
.

findings.scenario: The same Semgrep rule react-dangerous-html-review also flags SafeAnnouncement.tsx:7 for using dangerouslySetInnerHTML, producing a second warning alongside the exploitable note sink.
findings.impact: None: the rendered markup is a fixed scheduled-maintenance banner that ships inside the application bundle and never varies at runtime.
findings.evidence: Disproved by source: the injected string is the module-level const trustedAnnouncement defined at SafeAnnouncement.tsx:1 with no interpolation, props, state, or user input anywhere in the file; the HTML is static and source-controlled, so no runtime data can reach the sink. This proved false positive is retained in the codebase and dismissed here rather than silenced, per the review brief.

findings.scenario: A keyboard-only user tabs through the work queue and can neither focus nor activate any row: the PR replaced the native button element with a div that only responds to onClick.
findings.impact: The entire queue becomes mouse-only; keyboard and screen-reader users cannot select work items, and assistive technology no longer announces rows as interactive controls.
findings.evidence: Verified in the review head: WorkQueue.tsx:16 renders <div onClick=...> with no role, no tabIndex, and no key handler, while the base side of the protected diff shows the element was <button type="button">; restoring the native button element restores focus order plus Enter and Space activation and button semantics for keyboard users.
findings.fix: Render queue rows as native <button type="button"> elements with the existing className, key, and onClick in src/components/WorkQueue.tsx.

findings.scenario: Clear the Reviewer note or type fewer than eight characters and activate Save draft; the head button is only disabled while saving, so a short note is submitted immediately.
findings.impact: Empty or near-empty reviewer notes reach the server and persist on the work item, destroying the audit quality that the client guard previously enforced before submission.
findings.evidence: The protected diff removes disabled={saving || note.trim().length < 8} and the explicit type from the save button at ActionComposer.tsx:48, and the head server also lost its note-length check, so nothing rejects a short note anywhere; the fix restores the client disabled guard with type="button" and the server-side meaningful-reviewer-note validation.
findings.fix: Restore disabled={saving || note.trim().length < 8} and type="button" on the save button in src/components/ActionComposer.tsx, and restore the eight-character note guard in src/server/reviewPolicy.ts.

findings.scenario: Submit a draft with status Ready and a note merely containing the word approved for a Blocked or Escalated work item; the early return at reviewPolicy.ts:4 skips every remaining server guard.
findings.impact: Approval wording becomes an authorization bypass: blocked and escalated work reaches Ready without evidence requirements, and note-length validation is disabled server-wide for any note containing the magic word.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on the review head: assertAllowedTransition({ status: 'Blocked' }, { note: 'approved by reviewer', status: 'Ready' }) returns without throwing, exactly the case the protected reviewPolicy.test.ts expects to throw /cannot transition/; the client additionally coerced High-priority drafts to Ready before sending (ActionComposer.tsx:18-19 in the head), so the fix removes the server early return, restores the note-length guard, and deletes the client normalization so blocked or escalated items can never reach Ready by wording.
findings.fix: Delete the approved early return in src/server/reviewPolicy.ts, restore the eight-character meaningful-note guard ahead of the Blocked/Escalated to Ready rule, and remove the client-side normalizedStatus coercion in src/components/ActionComposer.tsx.
